links.reading: Beatrice, you make Athena’s questions welcome, especially during the Sunday call. Athena may grow bolder about asking and trying again when you include her in the conversation. Keep your answer warm and simple, so she can follow it and stay involved. Behaviour check: On your next Sunday call, notice whether Athena asks another question after you welcome the first.

Beatrice, your encouragement can help Athena stay with a small effort instead of giving up. When a drawing or toy feels difficult, you can make trying again feel worthwhile. Athena may show you more determination when you notice the effort, not only the finished result. Behaviour check: During play this week, praise one attempt and see whether Athena chooses to try again.

Beatrice, when the tablet goes off, you may explain the limit while Athena is still reacting. Athena may not be ready to take in more words, even when your reason is clear. This is the challenge: give one warning, then one next step, so she can act without another long exchange. Behaviour check: At the next tablet transition, see whether one short warning helps Athena move on.

Beatrice, you may want a clear plan when Athena is upset, while she may need time before she can follow it. If you push for an answer too soon, both of you can feel stuck. Keep the limit steady and offer one small choice, so Athena can settle without losing the boundary. Behaviour check: During the morning rush, try one choice and watch whether Athena can take the next step.

Beatrice, your quick response can help Athena turn a small task into play. She may be more willing to join when you give her something she can do herself. Let her try before you step in, so she can build confidence through practice. Behaviour check: While tidying before dinner, give Athena one small job and see whether she wants another.

Beatrice, you often notice when Athena needs comfort, even before she has found the words. A soft voice or a quiet pause may help her settle. Check what she needs before adding more reassurance, so you respond to this moment rather than guessing. Behaviour check: At bedtime, pause once and see whether Athena asks for comfort or quiet.

Beatrice, you may want to soothe Athena quickly when she is upset, but she may need something simpler than extra comfort. Guessing can leave you doing more while she stays unsettled. Ask one clear question, then wait for her response, so you can learn what helps her now. Behaviour check: At bedtime this week, ask what Athena needs before offering another comfort.

Beatrice, Athena may change direction quickly when a familiar plan ends, and your explanations may not settle her right away. At the tablet transition, she may need a clear cue before the screen goes off. Keep the change predictable, so she can practise moving on without a surprise. Behaviour check: Give Athena one warning before the tablet ends and notice how she responds.

Beatrice, Athena’s distress can reach you deeply, especially at bedtime. You may feel pulled to fix the feeling at once, though she may only need a quiet minute beside you. Keep your voice low and stay nearby, so she can settle without carrying your worry too. Behaviour check: When Athena calls again at bedtime, answer briefly and see whether she needs you to stay.

Athena, you can bring out Beatrice’s playful, attentive side simply by being yourself. She may watch your face closely and join your games with warmth. Beatrice, let her lead for a little while, so you can enjoy what she chooses without turning it into a lesson. Behaviour check: This week, notice what game Beatrice joins when Athena starts it.

Athena, your affection may make Beatrice want to give comfort and make things feel settled. She may show care through a familiar snack, a soft voice, or staying close. Beatrice, let the simple gesture be enough, so you can care without trying to make every upset disappear. Behaviour check: At bedtime, notice whether one familiar comfort helps Athena settle.

Athena, your feelings may be easy for Beatrice to notice, even when other people are nearby. She may become especially attentive when you protest or ask for help. Beatrice, offer comfort without making Athena perform for anyone, so she can be upset and still feel safe. Behaviour check: When Athena is upset in front of family, see whether a quiet response helps.

Beatrice, your care can help Athena feel safe through familiar routines and small comforts. A calm voice or the same bedtime steps may matter more than a long explanation. Keep those comforts steady, so she can learn what to expect when she is tired. Behaviour check: Follow the usual bedtime steps and see which one helps Athena settle.

Beatrice, you can make Athena curious by talking with her about the small things around you. A question on the Sunday call may turn into a lively exchange. Follow her interest before correcting or redirecting, so she learns that speaking up brings connection. Behaviour check: On the next Sunday call, follow one question Athena asks and see where it leads.
